description.narrative: Insatsen är den sista fasen i ett långt bilateralt samarbete mellan de statistiska centralbyråerna i Albanien och Sverige. Insatsens mål är att bidra till att INSTAT uppfyller EUs krav för produktion av statistik och för användares behov i Albanien. Det generella syftet med samarbetet är att bidra till att utveckla ett hållbart statistiskt system i Albanien, där INSTAT förstår sitt behov att självständigt bygga intern och extern kapacitet samt att producera användarvänlig statistik som är till nytta för deras huvudaktörer och allmänheten.Åtgärden faller under resultatområde 2 i Sveriges strategi för Albanien och det rör sig om de albanska institutionernas förbättrade kapacitet som Albanska statistikinstitutet (INSTAT) för att få större inverkan och uppnå mer hållbara resultat i Albanien, till exempel att förbättra politiken för att förbättra styrningen och därmed levnadsvillkoren för det albanska folket. Insatsen kommer att pågå i tre år med start i januari 2018 till december 2020, med en total budget på 19 426 710 SEK. SCB är implementerande partner som huvudsakligen är ansvarig för budgethantering och rapportering. Projektet förutsätter stöd för att producera miljöstatistik, samt uppdelning av olika statistik per kvinnor och män.

The intervention is a last phase of a long-term bilateral cooperation between the Albanian and Swedish national statistical offices. The intervention aims to help Albania’s Institute of Statistics (INSTAT) to fulfil the EU requirements for statistical production and the needs of the users in Albania. The overall objective of the cooperation is to contribute to the development of a sustainable statistical system in Albania, where INSTAT understands its true needs and independently builds internal and external institutional capacity and produces statistics that are user-friendly and used by key stakeholders. The intervention falls under the result area 2 of the Sweden strategy for Albania and it relates with the improving capacities of Albanian institutions as Albanian Statistics Institute (INSTAT) to make greater impact and achieve more sustainable results in Albania, such as enhancing policy-making to improve governance and therefore the living conditions for the Albanian people. The intervention will last for three years, starting from January 2018 until December 2020, with an overall budget of 19 426 709 SEK. The implementing partner primarily responsible for budget execution and reporting is Statistics Sweden (SCB). The project foresees support on producing environmental statistics, as well as disaggregation of various statistics per women and men.

To contribute to the development of sustaniable statistical system in Albania where the National Albanian Statistical institution (INSTAT) understands its true needs and independently builds internal and external institutional capacity and produces statistics that are user-friendly and used by key stakeholders. The specific outcomes for the intervention areas are: 1. Management INSTAT managers and staff will be better able to plan, organise and prioritise work with improved communication, involving staff in planning, decision-making and monitoring using a coaching-based approach. INSTAT will be considered as a learning organisation and a provider of knowledge of the statistical system. 2. Statistical Methodology INSTAT will have the capacity to produce and improve existing statistics independently according to EU requirement and the European Statistical Code of Practice and to develop new statistics with sound methodology. INSTAT will also have increased capacity in combining different data sources (administrative and surveys) for producing official statistics and have a system for data confidentiality in place. 3. Information Technology INSTAT will have the capacity to maintain servers and back-up systems and to develop standards for communications.

The achievements in 20 years of cooperation are expected to be sustainable. The institutional capacity of INSTAT is improved and the institution will be able to support the national statistical system in the future. It is noted through users' survey, the trust and use of official statistics by key stakeholders and the public is increasing year by year. The government uses official statistics in policy making, for monitoring the 2030 Agenda and to support the EU negotiation process. The number of visits on INSTATs website was 4 362 864 in 2021, compared to 1 300 061 in 2017. In addition, the index level of users' satisfaction with a scale 1-5, has increased from 3.22 (in 2017) to 3.88 (in 2021). The compliance of the statistics with the EU requirements is a corner stone in the EU accession negotiations. Between 2016 and 2020, the number of data points measured by Eurostat in this respect increased by 116 percent. The level of compliance with the five-year Albanian Official Statistics Program (OSP), has also increased, with 6 percent compared to the baseline in 2018. On the management component, a framework for measurable indicators (Performance Assessment Framework, PAF) has been implemented and is now in full use in the organization. A platform for HR and an intranet has been developed and improved the efficiency and the internal communication of INSTAT. The reporting of statistics to the EU has been strengthened when it comes to social statistics, forest statistics, and environment statistics. A planning and following-up tool has been developed and implemented in order to facilitate the management of the statistical production. A management system for information security has been implemented and the staff capacity in hardware, software and security routines have been improved. A platform for transferring data from the tax authority to INSTAT has been developed and is now in use, which has greatly improved efficiency of the statistical production at INSTAT. The platform for micro data aimed at researchers, SIMONA, has been developed and launched for external users. It is now in use by several research projects.
